insight.title: Why the Straightest Path is Rarely the Best Choice
insight.subtitle: How trying to solve a problem directly creates more resistance
insight.notificationHook: Straight lines cause most of our friction

sections.text: Rivers never flow in straight lines because straight paths build destructive speed. By bending and meandering, a river safely dissipates its kinetic energy, allowing a rich ecosystem to grow along its curves.

In decision-making, we often force straight-line solutions to speed things up. Pushing directly against a difficult problem creates immediate resistance, leading to stress, friction, and ultimately, compromises that weaken your original vision.

True innovators avoid direct confrontation. By taking a slightly indirect path—like running a low-stakes test instead of demanding instant approval—you bypass natural resistance and discover better, more creative solutions.
Try this today: When you face a stubborn problem today, think of one small detour instead of pushing through.
Force creates friction, but detours create options.
